STRAP-GEOM: Shoulder straps run from the yoke node to a shoulder-crest point 90 mm to each side, 100 mm fore and 40 mm above it (yoke 50 mm below C7, geometry.yaml datums); the lifter runs from its node to the same point (its strap end sits just fore of the crest): 42-46 deg below horizontal against geometry.yaml's 40.6. Webbing cables, tension only, EA from poly_webbing_25mm (WEB-EA).
T1(c) on the rig: photograph the strap and lifter angles at 225 lb; re-run with the measured angles.
STRAP-K: The body under each shoulder crest = the HA-LS-1 shoulder + lifter springs per side (2, 7, 6.5 N/mm x, y, z) and 4x that, as a band; the path is reported for both.
T1(c): crown-top sag against load at 25 % steps; the measured secant stiffness picks the band end.
STRAP-SLING: With the hipbelt off the shoulder strap is a sling: its front run (crest -> lower adjuster -> lower anchor, geometry.yaml shoulder_strap_lower_anchor z 110) is snug and carries tension; modelled as a straight cable crest -> nearest stay node. Run with and without it.
T1(c): crane scale on one lower strap at 225 lb.
LIFT-T: Lifter tension at the factored load is set by how hard the wearer cinches it; swept 0 / 200 / 450 / 700 N each (700 = the linear spring model's lifter reaction).
T1(c): crane scale in each lifter at 225 lb (record the tension).
BACK: With the hipbelt off the lumbar pad bears on the wearer's lower back (on the rig: the hip log), compression only, 30 N/mm in total (HA-LS-1 lumbar_pad ky).
T1(c) is run with the pad touching the hip log (belt unbuckled); a free-hanging variant is in T1(c)-sway.
WEB-EA: Webbing linear to break: EA = 13344 N / 0.15 = 89 kN (secant); 25 mm polyester record.
Pull a 300 mm length of the lifter webbing on the crane scale to 500 N and read the stretch.
IMP: Imperfection = the linear first buckling mode of the real crown (the 0.54 mode) scaled to 4 mm at its largest node translation (about crown height / 200), and 8 mm as a check.
First-article frame: measure crown-top and stay-foot out-of-plane against a straight edge before T1.
DEAD: The C8 loads stay as HA-LS-1 places them (dead nodal loads on the bag nodes, bag couple on TB0/TB2 and the stay feet); only the supports are made physical.
Not a test item: it is the standard's load.

PAWL-LIFT: The release cord swings the pawl 10 deg about its pin (7.9 deg lifts the nearer tooth tip 0.5 mm clear of the rack tips, + 2 deg).
Pawl dry fit in the first print: pull the cord to the stop, rack slides.
PAWL-PLACE: Pivot 20 mm below the teeth (pawl line z 520 -> pin z 500), pin 4 mm fore of the rack tooth tips (printables.spring_pawl pin at (4, 4) with the tooth face 0.15 mm above the rack tips).
Pawl dry fit: teeth seat in the rack with the pin in its sleeves.
PAWL-SPRING: The LP pawl's spring is a 0.5 mm music-wire torsion spring on the pin beside the pawl (3 mm a side in the 22 mm channel), one leg on the 10.5 mm tang, the other on the window's lower edge; the old 14 mm tang does not fit the housing.
Pawl dry fit + 100 release cycles by hand.
PAWL-FDM-STRENGTH: The LP pawl keeps the teeth, the pin and a 7.5 mm arm (old 8): the rack check (printables.rack_check, rating 5328 N) is on the teeth and is unchanged; the arm only carries the spring.
Rack/pawl pull test in the test kit (unchanged).

rig.run_spine_end: anchored to a stub of the OD 20 spine tube 25.0 mm fore of the bar axis, the 6.0 mm collar fitted (BL-046 geometry); the run then pulls fore-down by itself

tl1.note: TL-1 proofs the bound or the vector? The bound (run in line with the guy) is not a physical pull on BL-046's geometry (the run now heads fore, the guy aft); the proof is set on the larger of the BL-046 vector and BL-045's published 497 N, so it never drops below the released value.
